questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo with insufficient depth of field. Dr. REDA advises him to adjust his settings. To increase depth of field in dental photography, which parameter should be modified?
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'To increase depth of field, you need to close the aperture (f/22 or f/32). This allows the entire tooth and surrounding tissues to be sharp.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will switch to f/22!'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of a dental arch. Dr. REDA tells him: 'There are teeth missing in the photo!' What is the likely problem?
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'An incorrect shooting angle can cut off the dental arch. The camera should be positioned perpendicular to the arch.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will check my angle.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA shows Dr. RACHID a photo with shadows under the teeth. He asks: 'How to avoid these shadows?' Dr. RACHID thinks.
options: Use a second flash to eliminate shadow areas
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Shadows are caused by unidirectional lighting. A second flash or a ring flash provides uniform lighting.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will invest in a second flash.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a smile photo with a yellow cast. Dr. REDA asks him: 'Did you set the white balance?' Dr. RACHID replies: 'No, it was on automatic.' What should he do?
options: Set white balance manually with a color chart
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Automatic white balance can be fooled. Manual white balance with a color chart guarantees faithful colors.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will switch to manual.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA examines a post-operative photo. He tells Dr. RACHID: 'The gum looks too red.' Dr. RACHID asks: 'Why?' Dr. REDA replies:
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Excessive saturation can make gums abnormally red. Saturation should be adjusted sparingly.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will reduce saturation.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID must photograph a prosthetic preparation. Dr. REDA gives him advice. What is the most important parameter for this type of photo?
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'For a prosthetic preparation, precise focus is crucial to show details of the margins and preparation.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will use manual focus.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of the maxillary arch. Dr. REDA tells him: 'The photo is too dark.' Dr. RACHID asks: 'What should I adjust?'
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'You can increase flash, increase ISO, or open the aperture to brighten the photo.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will adjust the flash first.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA shows a frontal photo to Dr. RACHID. He asks him: 'What is the ideal proportion for a frontal photo?'
options: From hairline to chin, ears visible
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'The frontal photo should show the entire face, from hairline to chin, with ears visible to evaluate symmetry.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will respect this framing.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo with digital noise. Dr. REDA tells him: 'It's because of the ISO.' What ISO do you recommend for dental photos?
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'ISO 100-200 gives maximum image quality without digital noise. With good flash, it's sufficient.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will use ISO 100.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA explains to Dr. RACHID the importance of RAW format. Dr. RACHID asks: 'Why is RAW preferable to JPEG?'
options: RAW preserves all data for non-destructive editing
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'RAW preserves all raw sensor data, allowing non-destructive editing and greater latitude.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will always shoot in RAW.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID takes a photo of a patient with an asymmetrical smile. Dr. REDA asks him to check the patient's positioning. What is the likely cause?
options: Patient poorly positioned relative to the camera
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Incorrect patient positioning can create asymmetry. The patient must be perfectly frontal.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will recenter the patient.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA must photograph a tooth with a composite restoration. Dr. RACHID asks him: 'What is the particular challenge of this type of photo?'
options: Managing translucency and reflections of the composite
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Composites can be translucent and reflective. You need to manage lighting and angles to capture the texture.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will work on my angles.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of the mandibular arch. Dr. REDA tells him: 'There is a shadow under the tongue.' How to avoid it?
options: Use a tongue retractor or adjust the flash angle
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A tongue retractor or adjusting the flash angle can eliminate shadows under the tongue.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will use a retractor.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA must train interns in dental photography. In his opinion, what is the most important skill to master?
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Mastery of manual settings is fundamental to control every parameter and obtain quality images.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will practice in manual mode.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a frontal photo of a smiling patient. Dr. REDA tells him: 'The smile is forced.' How to get a natural smile?
options: Engage in conversation and capture the spontaneous smile
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A spontaneous smile is obtained by engaging the patient in conversation, making them laugh or talk.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will create a relaxed atmosphere.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA shows a profile photo to Dr. RACHID. He asks him: 'What should I control on a profile photo?'
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A profile photo allows evaluation of lip relationship, chin profile, and aesthetic line.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will analyze these parameters.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of a dental implant. Dr. REDA asks him to check the sharpness of the photo. What is the correct setting for photographing an implant?
options: A closed aperture (f/22-f/32) for great depth of field
A wide aperture (f/2.8) for an artistic effect
A high ISO for more brightness
A slow speed to capture details
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'For an implant, you need a large depth of field to see all the details of the threads and interface.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will close the aperture.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA explains to Dr. RACHID the importance of contrast in dental photography. Dr. RACHID asks: 'How to improve contrast?'
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Contrast can be improved by adjusting tone curves or contrast in editing software.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will learn to use curves.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a frontal photo of a patient. Dr. REDA tells him: 'The image is too contrasty.' What should he adjust?
options: Reduce contrast in post-production or adjust lighting
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Excessive contrast can be reduced in post-production or by modifying lighting.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will reduce contrast in editing.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA asks Dr. RACHID: 'What is the advantage of ring flash over standard flash?' Dr. RACHID thinks.
options: Ring flash provides shadow-free lighting and a light ring
Ring flash is easier to use
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Ring flash provides uniform, shadow-free lighting and creates an aesthetic light ring.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will invest in a ring flash.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of a tooth with a cavity. Dr. REDA asks him to take a more detailed photo. Which setting should he adjust?
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'For more detail, increase the reproduction ratio, for example to 2:1 or use a lens with greater macro capability.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will get closer.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA explains to Dr. RACHID that sharpness is crucial. Dr. RACHID asks: 'How to improve image sharpness?'
options: Use a tripod and manual focus
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A tripod stabilizes the camera and manual focus allows precise control of the sharpness zone.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will use my tripod systematically.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of a tooth with a metal restoration. Dr. REDA tells him: 'There are too many reflections.' How to manage metal reflections?
options: Use a polarizing filter and adjust the flash angle
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'The polarizing filter and adjusting the flash angle reduce reflections on metal surfaces.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will equip myself with a polarizer.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA must create a photographic protocol for his practice. Dr. RACHID asks him: 'What photos should be included in the standard protocol?'
options: Front view, profile view, dental arches, and specific details
Only the photo of the problematic tooth
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'The standard protocol includes a front view, a profile view, views of the maxillary and mandibular arches, and specific details.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will formalize this protocol.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID, after having mastered the basics of dental photography with Dr. REDA, receives his congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. RACHID?
options: Become an expert in dental photography and train others
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Mastery of dental photography is a valuable skill. Training others is the next step.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will share my knowledge.'
